data.narrative:
Basecamp Research, a Series B biotech & health company founded by Oliver Vince and Glen Gowers, has raised $85M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of 4 private peers at Series B/C stage (Eikon Therapeutics, Colossal Biosciences, Chai Discovery, New Limit) plus 3 public biotech names (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L).

Two valuation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement to the $85M raised proxy, yielding $162M. Peer-median analysis across the 4 same-sector comparables produces $3.5B, reflecting a wide range from $539M (Eikon) to $10.3B (Colossal). Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiple (9.2x median across public Biotech & Health) cannot be applied absent revenue disclosure. Triangulating the two methods produces a valuation range of $137M (low), $1.8B (median), and $4.0B (high).

The wide dispersion reflects material stage and outcome uncertainty within the peer set. Stage-progression yields a conservative floor based on capital deployed. The peer-median implies substantial upside but depends critically on which comparable—early-stage (Eikon at $539M) or later-stage leaders (Colossal at $10.3B)—most accurately reflects Basecamp's positioning. Revenue, clinical progress, and intellectual property scope remain key value drivers not quantified here.
